newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies expected lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies expected lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open 0.200 to 0.300 cent a lb lower while pork bellies were called 0.250 to 0.500 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Most analysts expect sharply lower cash hog and pork prices to weigh heavily on hog futures early despite a late recovery in futures Tuesday. Early cash hog markets are weaker than expected and a forecast upcoming seasonal break in loin prices will likely weigh heavily on trade sentiment, they said.
Producers are shipping more hogs than expected after the last Hogs and Pigs report, they added.

The increased hog runs and slaughter as well as falling cash belly prices were seen pressuring pork belly futures despite late support Tuesday on talk of an oversold condition. The weekly CME out-of-town storage report was also considered slightly bearish, analysts said.
The report showed a net in-movement of 130,000 lbs into warehouses outside Chicago in the latest week versus trade expectations of a net out-movement of 500,000 to 1.25 million lbs.
February futures have fallen 1,030 points from last week and could extend this break if the market again turns technically very weak, analysts added.
